acceptance: Red test first: the llm-calls.ndjson of cycle 2035 as a fixture; with max_llm_minutes 90 the decision at each boundary is none until the sum passes 90 (after audit round 2) and stop after it.
Each limit (max_llm_minutes 90, max_fresh_tokens 2500000, max_cache_read_tokens 40000000, max_audit_rounds 2) gives a stop alone, and the decision names the limit and the value.
At shadow the decision is would_stop, and CYCLE_SPEND_LIMIT is recorded once for each cycle.

Each key refuses a value outside its range with the key name: 9 and 601 for max_llm_minutes (10..600), 99999 and 20000001, 999999 and 500000001, 0 and 5. workflow.cycle_spend.stage is a strict stage key (off, shadow, enforce; default shadow).
fix: Add a pure package cyclespend that sums llm-calls.ndjson of a cycle and its audit_dispatches and compares them with workflow.cycle_spend. It returns the decision none, would_stop or stop with the limit and the value. The orchestrator asks it at each phase boundary only, so a limit crossed inside a phase stops the cycle at the next boundary.
notes: Rank 4: the backstop for each miss of ranks 2 and 3. Not workflow.cycle_budget, which is the stage of the loop end decision (package cyclebudget). The call site in internal/core is on the fence, so the console item wire-cost-aware-repair-call-sites wires it after this item lands.
routed_reason: console builds it as PR #1189 (rebased on main fixability); lane cycle 2043 built it twice
source: console, 2026-10-27, operator request on cycle 2035 ("balance to cost and output"). ADR-0158; plan docs/plans/cost-aware-repair-2026-10.md
summary: Cycle 2035 ran 3 h 36 min and 160.1 LLM minutes. Its lane deadline was 6 h 21 m 49 s, the 95th percentile of lane times, so no limit ended it. A 90 LLM minute budget stops it at 20:29Z after audit round 2 and saves about 70 LLM minutes. The shipped cycles of waves 141 and 142 used 28.9 to 47.0 LLM minutes.
title: A pure spend reader judges each cycle against a limit of LLM minutes, tokens and audit rounds (ADR-0158)
